# Preservation fixtures

Small `.xlsx` files that **contain the features the README promises are
preserved, not created**: data validations, conditional formatting, tables,
images, charts, pivot tables and comments/notes.

`test/corpus.test.ts` covers files we did not generate; this folder covers the
other half of the promise — the rich parts inside a file. Without these, nothing
proves that editing a cell does not silently drop a chart.

Generated by [`scripts/generate-preserve-fixtures.mjs`](../../../scripts/generate-preserve-fixtures.mjs)
and committed so `pnpm test` needs no build step.

## Inventory

| File | Size | Features it exists for | Rich parts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validations-and-conditional-formatting.xlsx` | ~6.4 kB | inline-list + `whole` data validations, `cellIs` + `colorScale` conditional formatting, a merged header, column widths | sheet-local (`xl/sharedStrings.xml`, `xl/theme/theme1.xml`) |
| `table-and-comments.xlsx` | ~8.1 kB | an `xl/tables/table1.xml` table with a theme style, two cell notes (`xl/comments1.xml` + legacy `vmlDrawing1.vml`), a rich-text note, a merge | `xl/tables/table1.xml`, `xl/comments1.xml`, `xl/drawings/vmlDrawing1.vml`, `xl/worksheets/_rels/sheet1.xml.rels` |
| `image-and-chart.xlsx` | ~9.4 kB | a 1x1 PNG (`xl/media/image1.png`) and a clustered **bar chart** (`xl/charts/chart1.xml`) plus its colour/style parts | `xl/media/image1.png`, `xl/drawings/drawing1.xml` (+ rels), `xl/charts/chart1.xml` (+ rels, `colors1.xml`, `style1.xml`), `xl/worksheets/_rels/sheet1.xml.rels` |
| `pivot-table.xlsx` | ~4.9 kB | a real **pivot table**: cache definition, cache records, the pivot table part and its relationship, wired from `xl/workbook.xml` | `xl/pivotTables/pivotTable1.xml`, `xl/pivotCache/pivotCacheDefinition1.xml`, `xl/pivotCache/pivotCacheRecords1.xml`, their rels |

## How they are built

- **ExcelJS** builds the first three: it can emit data validations, conditional
  formatting, tables, notes and images.
- ExcelJS **cannot emit charts** and has **no pivot support at all**, so the
  chart parts and the whole pivot package are written by hand into the package
  afterwards (`fflate`, already a runtime dependency).
- `pivot-table.xlsx` is hand-built end to end — small enough to read, and it
  keeps the fixture independent of ExcelJS quirks.

## Regenerating

```sh
node scripts/generate-preserve-fixtures.mjs           # rewrite the files
node scripts/generate-preserve-fixtures.mjs --check   # verify, exit 1 on drift
```

The output is **byte-deterministic**: workbook timestamps are pinned to fixed
dates, every ZIP entry is re-packed with one fixed MS-DOS mtime, and every
relationship id / drawing id / chart axis id is a literal in the script. Run it
twice and `--check` stays green; there are no random ids or "now" timestamps.

If you change the script, run `--check` (and `git diff`) before committing: a
fixture that drifts from its generator is a fixture nobody can reproduce.
